blocks.x: Winnipeg's rental market has loosened. Unfurnished one-bedroom asking rents have dropped three months running in [liv.rent's October 2026 report](https://liv.rent/blog/?p=69631), though still up 1.7% from a year earlier, and CMHC's latest survey put purpose-built vacancy at 2.8% in October 2025. When units sit, owners face the rent concessions vs renovations choice: discount the rent, or put the money into the unit.
What a rent concession really costs a Winnipeg landlord
One month free on a 12-month lease cuts your effective rent by about 8.3%. As a made-up illustration, on a $1,400 unit that's like leasing at roughly $1,283.

Under Manitoba's rent guideline (3% for 2027), a low starting rent is hard to recover, so a concession that keeps the face rent intact can make sense. But a concession doesn't fix why the unit isn't leasing, and it may have to be repeated at the next vacancy.
A quick decision guide
**Is the unit priced and presented like the competition?**
No → fix price, photos and description first.
Yes → keep going.
**Is the unit in worse shape than similar units nearby?**
No → a short, targeted concession may close the gap.
Yes → the unit is the problem. Renovate instead.
**Has the unit sat empty through more than one leasing cycle?**
Yes → a concession may only be a patch. Look at renovation.
When renovation beats a concession
The same money that buys a month free can often go toward upgrades that make the unit competitive for years. Get a written quote to compare. Upgrades worth pricing against a concession:
New flooring and paint where the wear shows most
A [kitchen](/services/kitchen-renovations) refresh: counters, hardware, lighting, faucet
A [bathroom](/services/bathroom-renovations) update, or in-suite laundry where feasible
A better entry, lighting and common areas

If a building was built or renovated before 1990, have old materials checked for asbestos before anyone disturbs them. Our guide covers [asbestos testing before you renovate](/blog/asbestos-testing-before-renovating-manitoba).
Choosing building renovation contractors
If you go the renovation route, the schedule matters as well as the quality, because every vacant day costs rent. Look for building renovation contractors who:
**Have a plan for occupied buildings,** so other residents know what to expect.
**Put the turn schedule** in writing.
**Check out on the public record:** WCB's clearance search, the Companies Office and the City's permit search, plus references.
**Handle permits** when work requires them.
**Standardize finishes** across units, so repairs stay simple.
Our [contractor checklist](/blog/how-to-choose-the-right-contractor-for-your-renovation-project) walks through each check.
If you do offer a concession
Tie it to a 12-month lease or longer.
Spread it over the lease rather than one free month up front.
Put a deadline on it to create urgency.
Write the terms clearly into the lease. In Manitoba, the details of a rent discount must be in the written tenancy agreement.
Plan the exit. Removing or reducing a discount takes three months' written notice.
Work out increases on the allowable rent, not the discounted rent you collect.
In a complex of three units or fewer, a discount in the first agreement after you regain the unit can't be more than 25% of the rent you set.
The bottom line
Concessions buy time. Renovations fix the reason the unit isn't leasing. When the unit is the problem, invest in the unit.
